scenarios.prompt: is this done and ready for review?
scenarios.preamble: No autonomy this session. Use no gh and no network.
assertions: Reader · No "what is X?": every PR, issue, follow-up, task, count, or label the reply names says what it is in the same breath or elsewhere in sight, so the reader could act on the reply without asking what something is; a plain merge option may name PRs the reply describes

Reader · Scannable: one bold lead line per thing the reader acts on (each PR, finding, option in the body, or running job), with its details under it or in the fold, while Next keeps its own format, only `a` bold; a reply about one subject passes with its headline and fact table, and a one-sentence answer passes as is

Reader · Grouped by the thing: everything said about one PR, finding, or job sits together under it, not spread across label rows such as Risk, Proof, or Queued that mix items; findings are grouped by severity, what must be fixed before cleanups

Reader · Brief: no paragraph of prose above the fold, the headline and notes above the closing under 60 words outside code, tables of at most six body rows, up to six items led by a bold name (an item counts only when its clause runs past 15 words), their group's bold label of at most 12 words, each item's first Decide, Review, or Do line of at most 25 words, a Do line's numbered steps, folds, and drafts (a scope-grill round counts its plan items and fold summary too), a fact table of at most five rows whose values run at most 25 words, and Next options of at most 12 words each that still name their items
Contract · Headline: the first line is a status marker (✅, 🟡, 🔴, or ⏳) and a bold outcome, answer, or question of at most 12 words

Contract · Next: a `---` line with blank lines around it sits directly above `Next` or `Done`, or, when only background work is left, the reply is or closes on one ⏳ line with a `then:` clause, with or without a `---` above it, and a `running` turn block; no `---` comes after it, and `Next`, when present, offers `a` and at most `b`, each naming its items briefly, never by a count alone

Contract · Turn block: the reply's last line is one `<!-- turn {…} -->` comment outside any code block, valid as `turn_block.parse` reads it, with `turn_block.picked` finding each option (a `stop` block lists `needs` and `options`; `running` and `done` may omit them); its `options` hold the same text as the Next options, its `needs` name what the reply waits on the reader for, and each option's `class` matches it (a call the reader decides is `decision` or a `stop:` class, not `routine`)
Fold: at most one, holding only what the reader may audit or compare, such as checks, sources, or the other options, and its summary leads with the worst result
Inline code: a code span holds only a name the reader would type or search, such as a command, path, or identifier; the rest is said in words
Once: each code block and draft appears once in the reply
The fold's summary leads with the worst check, a failure or a check that didn't run, and names those that didn't run, such as lint. The planted tests pass, because they expect the wrong header
